newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: LITHUANIA - DEALERS DIVIDED OVER BOURSE PROSPECTS.
newsitem.headline: LITHUANIA - DEALERS DIVIDED OVER BOURSE PROSPECTS.

text.p: Dealers are divided over when the Lithuanian bourse's Litin A index will reach the 3,000 mark again, according to a Reuters poll of seven brokerage houses active in the Lithuanian market.
The Litin A index, which tracks the bourse's 35 top listings, hit a high of 3,242.25 on January 17, more than doubling its value in late October when it was officially launched.
The index has since fallen to just over 2,600 as of Friday and most dealers were not bullish about its immediate prospects.
Three of the seven dealers polled said that they expected the index to claw its way back over the 3,000 mark in one to two months' time.
One said in three months' time while another said it should reach 3,000 by the end of the summer.
One dealer said by the end of the year while another said it would occur sometime this year but would not make a specific forecast.
"It depends a lot on Lithuania Gas, and it has some room to go up," said Tomas Andrejauskas of brokerage firm Suprema.
Some dealers complained that Lithuania Gas' value is weighted too heavily on the index, a situation which they said gives a distorted view of the market's actual progress.

"Foreign investors should be coming to the market in a big one soon," said one of the more optimistic dealers, who predicted that some of the players in the Estonian market would soon move their money south.
"Lithuania's market is larger than Estonia's and it has more options," he said.
"Most of the foreign newcomers who are looking at the Baltics are interested in Lithuania," said Kari Salonen, a broker with Williams de Broe in Helsinki.
But he said that bureaucratic obstacles were keeping some foreign investors out of the Lithuanian market.
"Making settlements and transfering shares is slow and expensive in Lithuania, especially compared to Estonia," he said.
He added that bureaucratic problems aside, Lithuanian shares looked very attractive right now.
"Lithuania has the best variety of listed companies in the Baltics with at least two or three from each sector," he said.
He also said that the market rose too high too fast in January and that it would probably not reach 3,000 again until the end of the summer.
Suprema, Vilniaus Bank, Litimpeks Bank, Snoras Bank, Vilfima, Mendes Prior Europe and Williams de Broe were the brokerage companies which participated in the poll.
